controllingAuthority.summary: The ordinary application route. Not more than 3 felonies total, not more than 2 assaultive-crime convictions in a lifetime, and not more than 1 felony for the same offence where that offence is punishable by more than 10 years; misdemeanours are otherwise unlimited. Deferred-and-dismissed cases count as misdemeanour convictions against those determinations. Relief is discretionary under MCL 780.621d(13) and (14). MC 227 is the SCAO-approved statewide form and MCL 780.621d(7) prescribes seven categories of required content without which the application is invalid.

exclusions: A felony, or attempt, punishable by life imprisonment.
Violations or attempted violations of MCL 750.136b(3), 750.136d(1)(b) or (c), 750.145c, 750.145d, 750.520c, 750.520d and 750.520g.
MCL 750.520e where the conviction occurred on or after January 12, 2015.

Traffic offences: operating while intoxicated by any person; any traffic offence by a commercial-endorsement holder committed while operating a commercial motor vehicle or otherwise a commercial motor vehicle violation; any traffic offence causing injury or death.
A felony domestic violence conviction where the person has a previous misdemeanour domestic violence conviction.
Human trafficking offences under MCL 750.462a to 750.462h and terrorism offences under MCL 750.543a to 750.543z.
Out-of-state and federal convictions, which are outside the act.

waitingPeriods.condition: More than one felony, from the last of sentence imposition, completion of felony probation, discharge from parole, or completion of imprisonment
One felony, or one or more serious misdemeanours, or one first-violation operating-while-intoxicated offence
One or more misdemeanours that are not serious misdemeanours, not a first-violation OWI and not assaultive

rules.filing: File in the convicting court. A separate application is required for each court; convictions may be combined on one application only if all are in the same court. Make five copies of the application and all attachments and take them to the clerk. Then mail the packet, fee and fingerprint card to Michigan State Police, Criminal Justice Information Center, Criminal History, PO Box 30266, Lansing MI 48909; a copy to the Office of the Attorney General, Assistance with Convictions and Expungements Division, PO Box 30212, Lansing MI 48909; and a copy to the correct prosecuting official.
rules.fees: $50 to the State of Michigan, sent to Michigan State Police. A fee may also apply for certified conviction records and for fingerprinting.
rules.notice: The Attorney General and each prosecuting attorney must be given an opportunity to contest under MCL 780.621d(10). Where the conviction was for an assaultive crime or a serious misdemeanour, the prosecuting attorney notifies the victim, who may appear and make a written or oral statement.
rules.service: The participant serves by mail on MSP, the Attorney General and the prosecuting official, then completes the Proof of Service on page 3.
rules.participantSignature: Required. Subscribed and sworn before a deputy clerk or notary.
rules.notarization: Required, unless sworn before a deputy court clerk.

controllingAuthority.summary: SCAO form MC 262, Order of Acquittal/Dismissal or Remand, carries the notice that the defendant's fingerprints and arrest card will be destroyed by Michigan State Police within 60 days of the order when permitted by MCL 28.243, and the clerk must advise the MSP Criminal Justice Information Center of the disposition under MCL 769.16a. Under MCL 28.243(8)(b), where the prosecutor agrees at any time after dismissal, or where neither the prosecutor nor the judge objects within 60 days of the dismissal order, the arrest record, all biometric data and fingerprints are destroyed and any LEIN entry is removed. MSP acts on receipt of an appropriate district or circuit court order.

tracks.publicName: What a completed deferral means for clearing your record

controllingAuthority.summary: Three things are simultaneously true for a participant with a completed deferral. The case record is already nonpublic by operation of the deferral statute, so there is usually nothing to set aside on the court side. The arrest record may still exist and is addressed by the biometric-destruction routes rather than the set-aside act. And under MCL 780.621(2) the deferred-and-dismissed disposition counts as a misdemeanour conviction for determining set-aside eligibility, with MCL 780.621d(7)(d) requiring every such action to be listed on any application.
